Representatives from seven national laboratories, including both researchers and practitioners were present, as were federal representatives from NA-22, NA-80, NA-24, NA- 21, DTRA, DHS S&T, UK AWE and the UK Home Office. The workshop presented the state- of-the-art in terms of Radiological Data Fusion from the perspectives of LBNL researchers, the GRI commercial system, ORNL static sensor fusion, Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory- developed gamma/neutron data fusion algorithms, federal representatives’ perspectives, and a group discussion where the workshop participants discussed the preliminary findings from the scopingstudyandidentifiedpotentialstepsforfutureR&D.Thediscussionfocusedonthefollowing topics: • Need for evaluation metrics (how does one demonstrate the impact of SDF technology?); • New capabilities to inject synthetic contextual information (e.g., video) into a datastream; • Ease of use, which GRI’s experience training customers indicated was a lower barrier to entry for use than many expected; • Challenges of cost, complexity, and fragility; • Significant interest in further steps to quantify SDF data products and uncertainties; • Many mission-specific development opportunities including: LBNL Report #2001653 – the applicability of SDF for nuclear critical safety applications; – less constrained development (higher cost, size, weight and/or power); – more mission specific studies of the human-SDF impact (how does SDF-provided information improve decision making?); – appropriate levels of mission-specific detector system fidelity (imaging quality, energy efficiency, detection efficiency); – mission-specific algorithm development; – can we obtain detector performance requirements for missions; and – Customization of ML-based semantic data processing algorithms to support specific missions; • Multi-system SDF; • Change detection; • Digital twin creation; • Long collections: does SLAM drift cause issues? how to maintain real-time compute? can SLAM state of the art be improved? • Value of a shared development platform, by which the barrier to entry for development could be minimized; • DNNR&Deffortsshouldnotbeconstrainedbylevelsofcomputeavailableinmobilecomputers, but should assume compute resources continue to advances and research should delay compute compromise decisions for higher-TRL efforts; • The value of sophisticated post-hoc analysis pipelines for many applications; • Connecting SDF sensors/systems/post-processing to cloud compute; • The value of autonomous SDF-capable systems to perform measurements in scenarios where operators cannot; • Multimodal AI (Can such algorithms outperform ML-EM/MAP techniques?); and • The need for benchmark data to support development and evaluation. 4 SDF Applications The high-level missions and activities that were considered within this report include: ER missions ofDirectedSearch(Search), StabilizationandRenderSafe(SRS),post-detonationnuclearforensics (forensics),andactivitiesconductedbytheradiologicalassessmentprogram(RAP)teams;activities similartoNERmissionsconductedbyotherpartsoftheUSG,whichincludeDepartmentofDefense (DoD) forensics and search missions, and Department of Homeland Security (DHS)-supported steady-stateradiologicalmonitoring; nuclearsafeguards(safeguards)andnucleartreatyverification and compliance; support of nuclear facility operations (Ops) and nuclear facility decontamination and demolition (D&D); nuclear waste and waste facility management; nuclear contamination and remediation assessments; and NSDD and related port and border security, which domestically, fall under DHS umbrellas. Applications of environmental contamination assessment and clean-up; geological applications of radiation detection including material discovery and fault-line mapping; and space applications such as planetary physics, material discovery, and crew and equipment dose assessments have also been identified but are not further examined herein due to their limited application to DNN R&D end-users. In the following, we describe SDF applications and potential R&D needs as they relate to each of the DNN R&D missions.
